 This application coming on for admission this day, the co  following:
 ORDER

This is first bail application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant in connection with FIR/Crime No.267/2024 Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S. -
Bhanwarkua, District - Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(N), 376, 377, 384, 323 and 506 of the IPC.
2. Prosecution story, in brief is that prior to the incident, the prosecutrix and the applicant were known to each other.
On 03.11.2021, the applicant raped her by giving some intoxicated drink and he made an obscene video of the aforesaid act.
After this, the applicant raped the prosecutrix several times by threatening to make the said video viral.
He also committed anal sex with the prosecutrix.
The applicant took Rs.15,000/- from the prosecutrix earlier and Rs.80,000/- on 05.02.2024.
He also took her golden chain and earring.
Matter was reported on 06.03.2024.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that FIR was lodged belatedly by more than 02 years without any plausible explanation.
The prosecutrix is a major lady and she was Amaan Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106516560/

Therefore, prima facie, no alleged offence is made out against the applicant.
The applicant is a reputed person.
Police is trying to arrest him.
If he gets arrested, his reputation will be tarnished, therefore, it is prayed that he may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On other hand learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that gold chain an earring are to be recovered from the applicant.
Alleged cash which has been taken by the applicant from the prosecutrix is also to be recovered from him.
Custodial interrogation is required.
Therefore, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also considering the facts and circumstances, this Court is of the view that, it is not a fit case to grant of bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, M.Cr.C. is rejected.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shruti Amaan Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106516560/
